hakkinda.aciklama: UWin turns preparing a Windows installation USB into something that needs no technical knowledge. But its job doesn't end when the USB is written: it asks why you're installing, tells you what to do during setup, shows you which files will be erased, and leaves behind a guide you can read after the computer shuts down.
hakkinda.araclar.1: Restore a USB to normal — clears the installation-media structure that Windows' own format can't undo.
hakkinda.araclar.2: Health test — checks the drive really holds as much as it claims, catching drives with faked capacity.
hakkinda.araclar.3: Adding recovery tools to an existing USB, and this computer's hardware report.
hakkinda.guvenlik.1: The disk Windows runs from can never be selected.
hakkinda.guvenlik.2: Internal and large external disks are hidden by default.
hakkinda.guvenlik.3: If you pick a non-USB disk, you must confirm by typing its name.
hakkinda.guvenlik.4: The disk is re-verified before writing; if it changed, nothing happens.
hakkinda.guvenlik.5: After writing, the USB is read back; if it fails the check it is never called "ready".
hakkinda.ozellik.1: Lays out your computer's Windows 11 readiness item by item — and when something missing is just a setting switched off in the BIOS, it names that setting as your motherboard calls it. It asks why you're installing and tailors its advice to that. It counts and shows the files that will be erased on this computer.
hakkinda.ozellik.2: Downloads the ISO from Microsoft's own servers and verifies it with SHA-256. If you pick your own file, it looks inside to tell you which Windows it is and how large a USB you need.
hakkinda.ozellik.3: Decides UEFI/Legacy and GPT/MBR for you, and splits installation files over 4 GB. When writing ends it reads the USB back and verifies it — the silent write failure of cheap drives gets caught here, not in the BIOS.
hakkinda.ozellik.4: Shows the BIOS guide for your motherboard brand and writes it to the USB too. Leaves ready-made tools for repairing a Windows that won't start. When you're done, you can restore the USB to normal.

sirada.aciklama: Below is every screen you'll see, in order, after plugging in the USB. These steps were prepared for your computer. You can come back here any time.
sirada.baslik: What happens after the USB is ready?
sirada.bolum.bios: 1. Start the computer from the USB
sirada.kurulum.1.aciklama: The first screen asks for a language. Pick yours and press Next. For the keyboard layout, choose the one that matches the letters printed on your keyboard. You can change it later if you get it wrong.
sirada.kurulum.2.aciklama: It asks for a 25-character code. If you don't have one, don't worry: click "I don't have a product key" below. Windows still installs and works normally. You just get a small watermark, which disappears whenever you enter a key later.
sirada.kurulum.2.baslik: When it asks for a "product key"
sirada.kurulum.3.aciklama: You'll see a list: Home, Pro, Education. If you're unsure, pick Home — it's more than enough for home use. If your PC is already licensed, this screen may not appear at all, which is also normal.
sirada.kurulum.3.baslik: When it asks Home or Pro
sirada.kurulum.4.aciklama: It asks where to install Windows. You'll see rows like "Drive 0 Partition 1". Pick the largest one and press Next. Pressing Delete here erases everything on that row permanently — if you have files you want to keep, stop here and back them up first.
sirada.kurulum.4.baslik: The disk screen — pay attention here
sirada.kurulum.5.aciklama: A percentage counter starts. This takes 10-30 minutes. The computer restarts itself a few times — that's normal, don't touch anything. Once you see "Restarting", you can unplug the USB.
sirada.onizleme: This is a preview — the USB isn't ready yet
sirada.sonrasi.1.aciklama: Once setup finishes, connect to Wi-Fi or plug in a cable. Windows finds and installs most missing drivers (sound, network, camera) by itself. Go to Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates and repeat it a few times; that alone fixes most problems.
sirada.sonrasi.1.baslik: Get online and let Windows do the rest
sirada.sonrasi.2.aciklama: If you're going to play games or do video/design work, install the graphics driver yourself. Go to nvidia.com for NVIDIA, amd.com for AMD, or intel.com otherwise, and download from their Drivers section. Without it, games will stutter.
sirada.sonrasi.3.aciklama: If Windows Update didn't find everything, go to {0}, search for your board model and download the drivers. The audio and network (LAN / Wi-Fi) ones matter most.
sirada.sonrasi.3.aciklama.genel: If Windows Update didn't find everything, go to your motherboard or computer manufacturer's site, search for your model and download the drivers. The audio and network (LAN / Wi-Fi) ones matter most.
sirada.sonrasi.3.baslik: If sound or internet doesn't work
sirada.sonrasi.4.aciklama: If you have a product key, enter it under Settings > System > Activation. If this computer had a licensed Windows before, it usually activates by itself once online — you don't need to do anything.

tavsiye.genel.1: Back up the files you want to keep before installing.
tavsiye.genel.disk: On the disk selection screen, pick the largest partition and press Next. If you press "Delete", everything on that partition goes and cannot be recovered — if there are files you want to keep, stop at this step and back them up first.
tavsiye.virus.1: Before installing, back up the files you want to keep to an external drive — once setup starts there's no going back.
tavsiye.virus.2: If the computer has partitions other than C: (D:, E: and so on), format those too. If the virus reached them, it runs again the moment the new Windows starts.
tavsiye.virus.3: When setup is done, scan your backed-up files with Windows Defender before copying them back. Documents and installers can carry malware.
tavsiye.virus.4: Turn on Secure Boot in the BIOS. The one kind of malware that erasing the disk can't remove is the kind that settles in the boot layer; Secure Boot blocks it.
tavsiye.virus.baslik: To get rid of a virus
tavsiye.virus.disk: On the disk selection screen, pick the partition Windows is installed on and press "Delete". If you just press Next, the old Windows isn't erased — it's moved into a Windows.old folder, and the virus sits safely inside it, coming back the moment you copy your files out. That's why deleting here is essential.
tavsiye.yavaslik.1: Back up the files you want to keep before installing.
tavsiye.yavaslik.2: The disk itself may be the cause. If the computer is still sluggish afterwards, have the disk's health checked — old hard drives slow down as they wear, and a reinstall won't fix that.
tavsiye.yavaslik.3: When setup is done, don't reinstall every old program. The commonest cause of slowness is programs that run at startup.
tavsiye.yavaslik.disk: On the disk selection screen, pick the partition Windows is installed on and press "Delete". If you just press Next, the old Windows moves into a Windows.old folder that takes up half the disk — and the build-up causing the slowness isn't cleared either.
tavsiye.yenidisk.1: If the computer has more than one disk, make sure you picked the right one. You can tell them apart by size.
tavsiye.yenidisk.2: If your old disk is still connected, unplugging it during setup is safest — then there's no chance of installing onto the wrong one.
tavsiye.yenidisk.baslik: Onto a new or empty disk
tavsiye.yenidisk.disk: On the disk selection screen, pick the new disk. If it has partitions, delete them all, then press "New" and Next. Windows creates the partitions it needs itself.
tavsiye.yukseltme.1: The Windows.old folder is deleted automatically after 10 days. If there are files you want, copy them within that time.
tavsiye.yukseltme.2: You need at least 20 GB free on the disk — Windows.old takes room.
tavsiye.yukseltme.3: Your programs will be gone, your files will stay. Note down the installers and keys for your licensed programs before you start.
tavsiye.yukseltme.baslik: To move to a newer Windows version
tavsiye.yukseltme.disk: On the disk selection screen, pick the partition Windows is installed on and press Next directly. Don't touch "Delete" or "Format". Your old files move into a Windows.old folder and you can get them back from there.
